docs.title: Home
docs.text:
First login defaults

Wi-Fi HackCard-Setup / password hackcard2026 → http://192.168.4.1/ → Lab PIN 1234. Full table: Default Wi-Fi & PINs.

NFC: HackCard has a PN532 reader. It reads and writes external tags. It does not emulate a payment or access card — your phone cannot tap the board as if it were a contactless card.

docs.title: HackCard ESP32
docs.text:
Credit-card sized ESP32-S3 lab hardware — NFC, Wi-Fi, BLE, USB HID, and a browser Lab Console at http://192.168.4.1/.

Firmware v1.0.2

Start getting started

docs.title: Arduino example library
docs.text:
The HackCard library includes 73 standalone sketches. Each one teaches a single Lab Console feature (or a real-life demo) without loading the full web firmware.

Path in the repo:

HackCard_ESP32/HackCard_ESP32/library/HackCard/examples/

docs.title: How to run an example
docs.text:
1. Install the library: copy the HackCard folder to Documents/Arduino/libraries/HackCard, or open examples from the cloned repo.
  2. Arduino IDE → File → Examples → HackCard → pick a folder and sketch.
  3. Edit the // EDIT ME block at the top (PINs, URLs, SSIDs, text to type).
  4. Tools → same board settings as full firmware (First setup).
  5. Upload one sketch at a time (each .ino is a complete program).
  6. Open Serial Monitor @ 115200 and follow on-screen prompts.

Map the whole product

Start with 00_Start_Here/Web_Feature_Map — it prints which example matches each Lab Console area.

docs.title: Example folders
docs.text: Folder What you learn 00_Start_Here Feature map, custom app template 01_Basics RGB ring, buzzer, BOOT button, Wi-Fi LED — no Wi-Fi lab required 02_NFC Read UID, dump/write tags, Type 2 erase/clone/kill, MIFARE Classic labs 03_WiFi Scan, AP, STA, captive portal, beacon, training portal, monitor, karma, EAPOL capture 04_BLE Scan, advertise, GATT contact card 05_USB_HID Keyboard text, URLs, OS shortcuts, mouse, media keys, Ducky Script, desk workflows 05_Storage SD info, export folder layout 06_RealLife Badge tap, desk status, NFC lock/unlock, guest Wi-Fi notes, meeting helpers 07_System Profile/vCard, modes, diagnostics, activity log, Factory_Reset

docs.title: PINs and ethics in examples
docs.text:
• Sketches that erase, clone, or run Wi-Fi offensive demos may ask for a lab PIN — default 1234 unless you changed LAB_MODE_PIN in firmware.
  • Use only on tags, networks, and PCs you own or have written permission to test. See Authorized use.

docs.title: Default Wi-Fi, PINs, and URLs
docs.text:
Out of the box, firmware uses the values in HackCard_ESP32/config/user_config.h. Use these for your first login — then change them before sharing the board.

Change before demos, resale, or classroom handout

Defaults are public in this repository. Anyone nearby can join your AP or unlock Lab mode if you keep factory values.

docs.title: Quick first-time login
docs.text:
1. Flash firmware (First program).
  2. Join Wi-Fi: HackCard-Setup / hackcard2026.
  3. Browser: http://192.168.4.1/.
  4. Enter Lab PIN: 1234 to open full labs.
  5. Open Settings → set new AP password and Lab PIN → save.

To reset saved flash settings back to user_config.h, use example 07_System/Factory_Reset, then re-flash main firmware.

docs.title: Flash firmware
docs.text: Upload HackCard_ESP32.ino and confirm boot over Serial.

docs.title: Before upload
docs.text:
• Completed Install tools board settings
  • Optional but recommended: Personalize user_config.h
  • Correct COM port selected (unplug/replug if unsure)

docs.title: Upload steps
docs.text:
1. Open HackCard_ESP32/HackCard_ESP32/HackCard_ESP32.ino
  2. Sketch → Upload (or Ctrl+U)
  3. Wait for “Done uploading”
  4. Open Serial Monitor → 115200 baud
  5. Press RESET on the board if the log is empty

docs.title: Expected Serial output
docs.text:
You should see boot messages, peripheral init, and Wi-Fi AP startup. Typical lines include:

[boot] Starting RGB/buzzer after Wi-Fi settle time...

At the end of boot, note the SSID, password, and dashboard URL printed by firmware (defaults come from user_config.h):

Setting Typical default SSID HackCard-Setup Password (your AP_PASSWORD) Lab Console http://192.168.4.1/

Quiet serial?

With USB CDC On Boot, some hosts prefer the web Terminal in Lab mode. Serial should still show the boot banner at least once after reset.

docs.title: Quick hardware check (optional)
docs.text: Check Pass signal Ring Boot animation or status colors Wi-Fi SSID visible on phone (2.4 GHz scan) Browser After joining AP, http://192.168.4.1/ loads

docs.title: If upload fails
docs.text:
Symptom Try Port disappears Different USB cable/port; install CP210x/CH340 driver if needed “Failed to connect” Hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT; upload again Wrong partition Custom partition table + partitions.csv in sketch folder Compile errors Install all four libraries from First setup

More: monorepo HackCard_ESP32/HackCard_ESP32/docs/ARDUINO_SETUP.md and HackCard_ESP32/docs/WIFI_TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

docs.title: Install tools & connect USB
docs.text: Prepare your computer and connect HackCard for the first firmware upload.

docs.title: Step 1 — Connect HackCard
docs.text:
1. Use a USB-C cable that supports data (not charge-only).
  2. Plug into your PC. Windows should assign a COM port; macOS/Linux show a serial device.
  3. If no port appears, see Troubleshooting in Next steps.

Power is primarily from USB (board_config.h — USB power path).

docs.title: Step 2 — Install Arduino IDE
docs.text: Download Arduino IDE 2.x and install it.

docs.title: Step 3 — Install ESP32 board support
docs.text:
1. File → Preferences

  2. Additional boards manager URLs — add:

    https://espressif.github.io/arduino-esp32/package_esp32_index.json

  3. Tools → Board → Boards Manager → search esp32 → install esp32 by Espressif Systems

Use a recent 3.x core if available; match the monorepo’s ARDUINO_SETUP.md if upload fails.

docs.title: Step 4 — Install libraries
docs.text:
Tools → Manage Libraries — install:

Library Used for Adafruit NeoPixel RGB ring + Wi-Fi LED Adafruit PN532 NFC reader Adafruit BusIO PN532 dependency ArduinoJson Saved config / profile

docs.title: Step 5 — Get the firmware source
docs.text:
Clone or download the monorepo:

github.com/auratechkick/HackCard

Open this sketch in Arduino IDE:

HackCard_ESP32/HackCard_ESP32/HackCard_ESP32.ino

(From repo root: folder HackCard_ESP32, then inner HackCard_ESP32 sketch directory.)

docs.title: Step 6 — Board settings (before first upload)
docs.text:
In Tools, set at minimum:

Setting Value Board ESP32S3 Dev Module USB CDC On Boot Enabled USB Mode USB-OTG (TinyUSB) — required for HID lab Flash Size 4MB (32Mb) PSRAM OPI PSRAM Partition Scheme Custom partition table (uses sketch partitions.csv) Upload Speed 921600 (or lower if upload is unstable)

Full table: ARDUINO_SETUP.md.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: HackCard ESP32-S3 is a wallet-sized development board for hands-on security education: NFC tag work, controlled Wi-Fi labs, BLE demos, and USB HID exercises toward a host PC — all manageable from a built-in Lab Console web app.

docs.title: What you get in software
docs.text:
Piece What it does HackCard_ESP32.ino Full firmware — soft AP, REST API, embedded Lab Console HackCard library 73 standalone Arduino examples (NFC, Wi-Fi, BLE, HID, system) hackcard-web-ui HTML/CSS/JS source synced into firmware flash

You flash firmware over USB-C with Arduino IDE. Day-to-day control is usually Wi-Fi + browser at http://192.168.4.1/, with optional Serial Monitor @ 115200 or the web Terminal page.

docs.title: What HackCard is
docs.text: Capability Notes NFC read/write PN532 + PCB antenna — NTAG, Type 2 dump/clone labs, MIFARE Classic tools (authorized tags only) Wi-Fi lab Scan, AP, STA, captive portal, training portal, monitor, karma, capture — gated by Lab PIN BLE Scan, advertise, GATT contact card USB HID TinyUSB keyboard/mouse/media to a connected PC Feedback 12× WS2812 ring, Wi-Fi LED, piezo buzzer, BOOT button Storage Internal flash always; optional microSD for exports (Full Mode)

docs.title: What HackCard is not
docs.text:
• Not an NFC emulator — the PN532 is a reader/writer for physical tags.
  • Not a turnkey “hack any network” product — offensive-style tools are documented, PIN-gated, and for authorized labs.
  • Not 5 GHz Wi-Fi — ESP32 is 2.4 GHz only.
  • Not dependent on SD for the dashboard — the Lab Console is embedded in firmware; SD adds export folders and capacity.

docs.title: Business mode vs Lab mode
docs.text:
After you join the HackCard Wi-Fi and open the Lab Console:

Mode Experience Business Public-style digital profile (contact, QR, vCard). Labs stay hidden until you unlock. Lab Full sidebar (desktop) or bottom tabs (phone): Wi-Fi, NFC, BLE, HID, Files, Settings, Terminal.

Unlock uses LAB_MODE_PIN from config/user_config.h (default is a demo value — change before sharing the device).

Details: Open the Lab Console.

docs.title: Who this guide is for
docs.text: You are… Start here New owner — first flash What's on the board → First setup Backer / demo user Personalize → Lab Console Developer After this guide: monorepo HackCard_ESP32/docs/CUSTOM_DEVELOPMENT.md and library EXAMPLES.md

docs.title: Firmware version
docs.text:
Current release in this tree: 1.0.2 (FIRMWARE_VERSION in HackCard_ESP32/config/board_config.h).

Always treat board_config.h and user_config.h as authoritative for your checkout.

docs.title: Open the Lab Console
docs.text:
The Lab Console is the web app served at http://192.168.4.1/ when your phone or laptop is on the HackCard Wi-Fi access point.

UI source (for developers): HackCard_ESP32/hackcard-web-ui/www/ — embedded in firmware after sync; not loaded from SD.

docs.title: Default login (first boot)
docs.text:
Unless you changed user_config.h:

Item Default Wi-Fi SSID HackCard-Setup Wi-Fi password hackcard2026 Lab Console http://192.168.4.1/ Lab PIN 1234

Full list: Default Wi-Fi, PINs, and URLs.

docs.title: Connect in four steps
docs.text:
1. Power HackCard via USB-C (stable power for Wi-Fi labs).
  2. On phone or PC, open Wi-Fi settings and join the AP from the Serial boot banner (default SSID HackCard-Setup, password hackcard2026).
  3. Open a browser to http://192.168.4.1/ (use http, not https).
  4. If the phone shows a captive portal, accept the network, then open the URL manually if the dashboard does not appear.

Phone Wi-Fi tips

Use 2.4 GHz. Disable “5 GHz only” or aggressive auto-switching if the SSID never appears.

docs.title: Business mode → Lab mode
docs.text:
What you see first Meaning Digital profile Business mode — contact page, QR, vCard download Full sidebar / tabs Lab mode — all labs unlocked

To unlock Lab mode, enter LAB_MODE_PIN from user_config.h (or the PIN you set in Settings after a previous unlock).

On mobile, a PIN field may appear in the sidebar footer or in prompts before sensitive Wi-Fi/NFC actions.

docs.title: Lab mode — main areas
docs.text:
Area Typical use Dashboard Firmware version, Flash vs Full storage, AP IP, quick actions Wi-Fi Lab Scan, STA connect, AP settings, captive portal, training/monitor/karma/capture NFC Reader UID, tag info, dump/write, Type 2 tools, Classic labs Bluetooth LE Scan, advertise, contact card USB HID Type text, open URL, shortcuts — requires USB to host PC Files SD check, browse flash or SD, download/delete exports Settings AP password, Lab PIN, ring/buzzer Terminal Live log stream (similar family of messages as Serial @ 115200) Diagnostics Self-test style checks from the web

Desktop: left sidebar. Narrow screens: bottom tabs and More for extra pages.

docs.title: Storage tier on the dashboard
docs.text:
Tier Meaning Flash Mode No SD — labs run; SD export buttons disabled Full Mode SD mounted — Export to SD enabled for captures and dumps

Insert a FAT32 microSD before boot or use Files → Check SD card to mount.

docs.title: USB HID reminder
docs.text:
HID keystrokes go to the USB host (your PC), not the Wi-Fi client.

  • Arduino USB Mode must be USB-OTG (TinyUSB).
  • Plug USB-C into the PC, focus a text field, then use HID page buttons.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Wi-Fi monitor, karma, capture, and similar tools are for authorized education only. Change default PINs before demos.

Read: Authorized use.

docs.title: microSD folder layout (Full Mode)
docs.text:
When SD_AUTO_CREATE_FOLDERS is enabled, firmware creates lab export paths such as:

Path Typical content /nfc/exports/ NFC dumps /wifi/exports/ Scan logs, captures /logs/ Activity CSV /config/hackcard.json Optional portable overrides

Use Lab Console Files to browse without removing the card.

docs.title: Factory reset
docs.text:
To clear saved AP password, Lab PIN, profile, and lab files back to user_config.h:

  1. Upload Examples → HackCard → 07_System → Factory_Reset
  2. Confirm on device (BOOT / RESET as prompted)
  3. Flash HackCard_ESP32.ino again

docs.text: Symptom Check No COM port Data cable; driver; USB CDC On Boot: Enabled Wi-Fi SSID missing 2.4 GHz scan; read SSID from Serial banner Old UI after update Reflash firmware — UI is embedded, not on SD HID does nothing USB-OTG TinyUSB; cable to PC; text field focused Export buttons grey Insert FAT32 SD; wait for Full Mode on dashboard

docs.title: Personalize settings
docs.text:
Edit HackCard_ESP32/config/user_config.h before upload so Wi-Fi, profile, and security defaults match you — not factory demos.

After first boot, some values can also be changed from the Lab Console Settings page (stored in flash).

docs.title: Identity (Business profile)
docs.text:
Used for contact card, vCard export, BLE contact GATT, and example sketches:

Define Purpose USER_NAME, USER_TITLE, USER_COMPANY Profile header USER_EMAIL, USER_PHONE Contact fields USER_WEBSITE, USER_LINKEDIN, USER_GITHUB Links USER_BIO Short tagline

Example:

File: HackCard_ESP32/config/user_config.h

#define USER_NAME               "Alex Kim"
#define USER_TITLE              "Lab instructor"
#define USER_COMPANY            "Your organization"
#define USER_EMAIL              "lab@example.com"
#define USER_WEBSITE            "https://example.com"
#define USER_GITHUB             "https://github.com/auratechkick/HackCard"

docs.title: Wi-Fi access point
docs.text:
Clients (phone/laptop) join this network to reach the Lab Console:

Define Notes AP_SSID Default HackCard-Setup — pick something unique in a classroom AP_PASSWORD Min 8 characters — change before sharing AP_CHANNEL 0 = auto (2.4 GHz only)

2.4 GHz only

ESP32 cannot create a 5 GHz AP. On some phones, disable “5 GHz only” or “smart connect” if the SSID does not appear.

docs.title: Security — Lab PIN and vault
docs.text:
Define Purpose LAB_MODE_PIN Unlocks Lab mode in the browser; confirms sensitive actions VAULT_PIN Extra PIN for vault-style features where enabled

Defaults are for local demo only.

Change before resale or classroom handout

Set a strong AP_PASSWORD and a non-default LAB_MODE_PIN. Anyone who knows the defaults can unlock Wi-Fi and NFC lab tools on your AP.

docs.title: Comfort defaults
docs.text: Define Purpose DEFAULT_RING_BRIGHTNESS 10–100 DEFAULT_BUZZER_VOLUME 10–100 BOOT_ANIMATION Startup ring animation BUZZER_ENABLED Master buzzer switch ACTIVITY_LOGGING Activity log when storage allows CAPTIVE_PORTAL_ENABLED Captive portal behavior for training demos

docs.title: After editing
docs.text:
1. Save user_config.h.
  2. Re-upload HackCard_ESP32.ino (Flash firmware).

To wipe saved profile/AP/PIN back to this file’s values later, use library example 07_System/Factory_Reset, then flash main firmware again.

docs.title: What's on the board
docs.text: On-board hardware for HackCard ESP32-S3 (from config/board_config.h and PCB layout).

docs.title: On-board components
docs.text: Component Detail MCU ESP32-S3FH4R2 — 4 MB flash, 2 MB OPI PSRAM NFC PN532 + PCB antenna (I2C) RGB ring 12× WS2812 (GPIO 45) Wi-Fi status LED 1× WS2812 (GPIO 38) Buzzer Piezo, PWM (GPIO 37) microSD SPI (optional — enables Full Mode exports) USB-C Power and data (flash + USB HID to host) Buttons RESET (hardware) + BOOT (GPIO 0, user button in firmware) Front — RGB ring, Wi-Fi LED area Back — NFC coil, ESP32-S3, USB-C, SD slot

docs.title: What you supply
docs.text: Item Required USB-C data cable Yes — charge-only cables will not flash PC with Arduino IDE 2.x Yes — first firmware upload microSD (FAT32) Optional — large exports, /wifi/exports/, /nfc/exports/, etc. NFC tags (NTAG, etc.) For NFC tutorials — not included

docs.title: Flash Mode vs Full Mode
docs.text:
Mode When What changes Flash Mode No SD (or SD not mounted) Lab Console and labs run; Export to SD actions stay disabled Full Mode FAT32 SD inserted and mounted Export buttons enabled; Files page can browse SD

The dashboard shows which tier is active. You do not copy the web UI to the SD card — it ships inside firmware.

docs.title: Works without a microSD
docs.text:
• Boot animation, ring, buzzer, Wi-Fi AP
  • Lab Console at http://192.168.4.1/
  • NFC read/write to tags (exports may stay on flash or be limited)
  • USB Serial @ 115200 (boot banner shows SSID/password)
  • USB HID when connected to a host PC (with correct Arduino USB mode)

docs.text: → Install tools & connect USB

docs.title: Write your own sketch
docs.text:
You can use HackCard in two ways:

  1. Full firmware — HackCard_ESP32.ino + Lab Console (best for all-in-one demos).
  2. Custom Arduino sketch — #include <HackCard.h> and only the drivers you need (best for learning and single-purpose tools).

docs.title: Start from the template
docs.text:
Open 00_Start_Here/Template_Custom_App in the HackCard examples.

Typical pattern:

#include <HackCard.h>

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  RgbRing.begin(80);
  WifiLed.begin(70);
  Buzzer.begin(true);
  Buttons.begin();
  // Add only what you need: Nfc.begin(), etc.
}

void loop() {
  // Your logic
}

Remove unused peripherals to keep uploads small and behavior clear.

docs.title: Pin map and board config
docs.text:
Reference File Arduino library pins library/HackCard/src/HackCard_Pins.h Full firmware pins HackCard_ESP32/config/board_config.h Your name, AP, PINs HackCard_ESP32/config/user_config.h (full firmware only)

Examples use the library pin map — it matches the production board when you select ESP32S3 Dev Module with the project partition table.

docs.title: USB HID and SD helpers
docs.text:
After #include <HackCard.h>:

#include <HackCardUsb.h>  // UsbHid, Host, Ducky, HackSd — HID / Ducky / SD-heavy sketches

Requires USB-OTG (TinyUSB) in Arduino Tools.

docs.title: When to stay on full firmware instead
docs.text:
Need Use Browser Lab Console, REST API, web Terminal HackCard_ESP32.ino One feature, Serial-only, classroom step-by-step Library example or Template_Custom_App Change web UI layout Edit hackcard-web-ui/www/, sync into data/www/, reflash firmware

Developer guide in the repo: CUSTOM_DEVELOPMENT.md

docs.title: Suggested learning path
docs.text:
1. Flash full firmware and explore the Lab Console (Lab Console).
  2. Run Web_Feature_Map on Serial to see example names.
  3. Pick one folder (01_Basics … 07_System) and upload one sketch per day.
  4. Fork Template_Custom_App into your own .ino for a custom lab tool.

docs.title: Defaults reminder
docs.text: First login: Default Wi-Fi, PINs, and URLs.

docs.title: Authorized use
docs.text: HackCard is a security education and research platform. Wi-Fi, NFC, and USB HID features can affect networks, tags, and computers around you.

docs.title: You may use HackCard when
docs.text:
• You own the hardware, tags, and computers involved, or
  • You have written permission from the network/tag/system owner, or
  • You run a controlled lab or classroom with clear rules and consent.

docs.title: You must not use HackCard to
docs.text:
• Access networks, accounts, or data without authorization
  • Disrupt production Wi-Fi or impersonate real providers to harvest credentials outside a defined training exercise
  • Clone or modify payment cards, access badges, or credentials you do not own
  • Run USB HID payloads on machines without the operator’s knowledge

docs.title: Features that need extra care
docs.text: Feature Risk Mitigation Wi-Fi monitor / deauth demo RF disruption Your AP / your lab only; follow local law Karma / evil twin / training portal Misleading SSIDs Training only; disclose to participants NFC clone / Classic tools Tag copying Tags you own; comply with local law USB HID Keystroke injection Your PC only; informed users

docs.title: Before sharing or selling a device
docs.text:
1. Change AP_PASSWORD and LAB_MODE_PIN in user_config.h.
  2. Avoid training portal branding that mimics real companies.
  3. Ship a short “authorized use only” note with the board.
